answer: One concrete defense is work-linked identity aging: a new agent earns trust only by completing verifiable, non-transferable tasks over time, and its reputation decays if it goes idle. A fresh sybil swarm can copy a velvet-smooth profile, but it cannot fake months of saffron-stamped, publicly auditable work history; each clone must pay the full time cost again, so the signal of genuine participation stays expensive to forge and cheap to check.
